item.title: [7] Superconducting diode effect in magnetic superconductors realized by nonreciprocal domain-wall dynamics
item.description:
Last authors: Suk Bum Chung, Se Kwon Kim

Authors: Dong Hui Han, Suk Bum Chung, Se Kwon Kim

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant mechanism for magnetic superconductors potentially applicable to TRSB/magnetic topological systems.

Tags: #superconductivity #magnetism #transport

Abstract: The authors propose here a route to the superconducting diode effect through nonreciprocal magnetic domain-wall dynamics in ferromagnetic superconductors. Applied magnetic fields break time-reversal and inversion symmetries, producing direction-dependent critical currents for Walker breakdown—the onset of sustained domain-wall precession. Owing to the order parameter redundancy, the precession generates nonsingular phase slips. By connecting magnetic dynamics with superconducting transport, the authors identify a mechanism for realizing the superconducting diode effect without the need for complex heterostructures.

item.title: [7] Bulk signatures of reentrant superconductivity in UTe2 from ultrasound measurements
item.description:
Last authors: D. Aoki, J.-P. Brison, G. Knebel, and D. LeBoeuf

Authors: N. Marquardt, C. Duffy, C. Proust, S. Badoux, M. Amano Patino, G. Lapertot, D. Aoki, J.-P. Brison, G. Knebel, and D. LeBoeuf

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important experiment on unconventional superconducting candidate UTe2.

Tags: #unconventionalsuperconductivity

Abstract: The authors study here the field-reentrant superconducting phase of the unconventional superconductor UTe 2 using ultrasound measurements up to 77 T and down to 0.5 K. They find clear signatures of the field reentrant superconducting phase found for a field angle of 30 degrees from the b to the c axis in a longitudinal elastic mode, establishing the bulk nature of this superconducting phase. The authors observe an intriguing excess attenuation across the superconducting phase, which suggests unusual vortex dynamics and pinning mechanisms.

item.title: [7] Magnetoelastic mapping of the high-field phase diagram in the topological cubic helimagnet SrFeO3
item.description:
Last authors: Shintaro Ishiwata, Taka-hisa Arima

Authors: Masaki Gen, Shun Okumura, Shusaku Imajo, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental investigation of a topological magnetic material with significant electronic structure implications.

Tags: #topologicalmagnetism #experimental

Abstract: Here, the authors substantially update the high-field magnetic phase diagram of SrFeO 3 , which hosts a hedgehog–antihedgehog lattice. Most strikingly, they uncover a first-order metamagnetic transition into the forced ferromagnetic phase, accompanied by negative volume magnetostriction and dramatic elastic softening. These anomalous magnetoelastic responses signal changes in charge degrees of freedom, shedding new light on the role of ligand holes in helical magnetism.

item.title: [8] Correlated insulating states in twisted double bilayer graphene on CrOCl enhanced by interfacial charge transfer effect
item.description:
Last authors: Jian-Hao Chen, Mitali Banerjee

Authors: Ning Ma, Zekang Zhou, Chiara Cocchi, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of moire systems and interfacial effects on correlated states.

Tags: #moiré #graphene #correlatedelectrons

Abstract: Here, the authors investigate electrical transport in twisted double bilayer graphene (TDBG) on the antiferromagnetic material CrOCl (COC). At ultrahigh magnetic fields, an enhanced correlated insulating state is observed at half-filling of TDBG, which is attributed to the charge transfer effect between TDBG and COC. The authors further characterize the behavior of the correlated state by systematic temperature- and magnetic-field dependent measurements. Their results highlight the interfacial charge-related effect as a promising approach to manipulating the correlated states in moiré systems.
